title: Hard-coded maintenance backdoor exposes a remote shell
shows: The ARM ELF listens on 0.0.0.0:9090. XOR-obfuscated strings at offsets 0x46c and 0x474 decode with key 0xA7. The success path duplicates the accepted socket to stdin, stdout and stderr, then executes /bin/sh. Verify with readelf -S, objdump -d and xxd at the recorded offsets.
reason: The daemon starts at boot through etc/init.d/S65maint. A peer who knows the embedded command and password can obtain an interactive shell; remove the service or replace it with a properly authenticated management channel.

title: Clip-download service is exposed on the network
shows: The startup script launches clipstored with -d /mnt/sd/clips -p 8600; inspect the script and the usr/sbin/clipstored version banner.
reason: The service is enabled at boot and clipstored 1.2.0 is within DVS-2026-0107's affected range. Restrict access and update to a fixed version.

title: Cloud-sync credential is embedded in startup configuration
shows: The cloud-sync invocation contains --user svc --password tern-harbour-31 --host cloud.kestrel.example; inspect the script with grep or cat.
reason: A credential stored in a readable firmware file can be extracted by anyone with the image or filesystem access. Rotate it and replace static command-line secrets with protected provisioning.

title: Factory-default admin credential is documented and provisioned in the image
shows: The quick-start guide documents the factory admin login; usr/share/defaults/shadow.factory contains the same admin SHA-512 hash as etc/shadow. Verify with cat on both files and compare the admin hash fields; the documented password reproduces the hash using openssl passwd -6 with the recorded salt.
reason: The engine report cites only etc/shadow, which is a hash and does not itself reveal the default password. The separate quick-start document identifies the factory credential, and the factory shadow template carries the matching hash. Under the labelling rule F-02 is false as originally evidenced, while this independently evidenced default-credential exposure belongs in the missed-issues list. Rotate the credential and require unique per-device provisioning.
